subject: English
passage: Typically, conventional bioplastics are petroleum based, but environmental scientists searching for a truly sustainable alternative have used engineered Escherichia coli bacteria that secrete long chains of polylactic acid (PLA), forming a dense biopolymer film that functions like plastic packaging except in flexibility. The standard process for increasing flexibility involves high-temperature treatment, which consumes substantial energy and generates carbon emissions, so employing such a method would contradict the environmental benefits of the biopolymer approach. To address this, Dr. Sofia Lindqvist and colleagues worked to modify the E. coli bacteria to produce temperature-responsive proteins within the biopolymer structure, thereby allowing the material to achieve flexibility without external heat treatment.
prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?

choices.A: To illustrate how the researchers adapted the biopolymer approach to overcome a potential impediment to their main goal as presented in the text.
choices.B: To concede that the researchers' main goal as described in the text will be challenging to achieve due to the standard flexibility treatment being impractical for use on a biopolymer.
choices.C: To indicate the characteristic of conventional petroleum-based plastics that makes those plastics poorly suited to achieve the researchers' main goal as presented in the text.
choices.D: To describe a consideration that led the researchers to employ an alternative approach to treating a biopolymer that allowed them to achieve their main goal as presented in the text.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it accurately describes the function of the underlined portion. The researchers' main goal is developing a truly sustainable alternative to petroleum-based plastics. The underlined sentence explains that standard high-temperature flexibility treatment would 'contradict the environmental benefits of the biopolymer approach' because it consumes substantial energy and generates carbon emissions. This consideration directly motivated the subsequent action: 'To address this,' the researchers modified E. coli bacteria to produce temperature-responsive proteins, achieving flexibility without external heat treatment and thereby accomplishing their sustainability goal.
